explanation: The Almighty Creator who rules over heaven and earth, often referred to as the Father or the Lord in connection with Jesus' teaching about the kingdom of God.
The divine rule where God is king; a central theme in Luke 9 where Jesus proclaims that this kingdom does not come through outward signs but is already among the disciples.
The act of giving oneself to others, which Jesus emphasizes as the true path to greatness in God's kingdom by saying "the greatest among you shall be a servant".
The painful trials and death that Jesus predicts he must undergo; a necessary step before his resurrection and glory.
The event where Jesus is raised from the dead, confirming his divine nature and victory over death after three days in the tomb.
The twelve chosen men who followed Jesus; in Luke 9 they receive new instruction to prepare for suffering and are taught that no one can be master of him without first taking up their cross.
The symbol of the death Jesus must die, as well as a call to the disciples to deny themselves daily and follow in his footsteps through sacrifice and obedience.
The divine glory revealed when Moses and Elijah speak with Jesus on the mountain; a foretaste of the full kingdom to come after the suffering.
